clue.text: Moderation in drugs (not cocaine)

indicators.note: the bracketed 'not cocaine' tells us to strip the drug's letter out of the word before it

parts.note: medication is a collective word for drugs
C is the standard abbreviation for cocaine

explanation.surface: A plea for moderate drug use, with cocaine explicitly ruled out.
explanation.definitionFit: Mediation is calming intervention between parties, a sense of moderation as acting as a moderator in a dispute.

clue.text: On a voyage, ship's company is heard to chant

indicators.note: being heard means we take the sound of the words, not their spelling

parts.note: a ship's company is its crew; the 's makes it crew's
to chant is to sing

explanation.surface: Sailors singing aboard a ship at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is heard to' says CREWS SING, spoken, runs together: the S of CREWS merges with that of SING, so the first part is written CRUI.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone cruising is travelling by ship for pleasure, so is out on a voyage.

clue.text: Being theatrical under canvas

definitions.meaning: people ... sleep in tents, under canvas

explanation.surface: An actor showing off on a camping holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Camping is both exaggerated, showy behaviour and sleeping outdoors in a tent.

clue.text: Clever 23, one deep in the midst of ground crew

indicators.note: being in the midst of something puts these letters inside the other piece
ground here is the past participle of grind, so the letters are crushed into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
the deep is a poetic word for the sea

explanation.surface: A smart alec working among the ground crew at an airport.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 is DICK, so the definition reads 'Clever Dick'. 'ground' mixes CREW to give WCRE, with ISEA set inside after the W.
explanation.definitionFit: A clever Dick is a know-all, which is exactly what a wiseacre is.

clue.text: Starts to get lively during month of dance music

indicators.note: letters that happen during the month are set inside its name

parts.note: June is a month

indicators.note: the starts of the next words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Things start to liven up in the month of a big dance music festival.
explanation.definitionFit: Jungle is a fast breakbeat style of electronic dance music from 1990s Britain.

clue.text: Lenny, perhaps his last part after 'Chicken Run'?

indicators.note: his last letter comes after the other pieces

parts.note: a hen is a chicken
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

indicators.note: his refers back to Lenny, and his last part is the final letter of that name

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a comedian's final role might follow the animated film Chicken Run.
explanation.walkthrough: Lenny is the British comedian Lenny Henry; his name serves as definition and, through 'his', supplies its own last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Lenny Henry is a famous British comedian, so Lenny is an example of someone with this surname.

clue.text: Kind of green bananas

indicators.note: going bananas means going crazy, so the letters go wild

explanation.surface: A type of unripe banana.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' looks like the thing described as green, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A genre is a category or type of work, a sort or kind.

clue.text: Clean-cut doctor's description of former patient?

definitions.meaning: read as three words, ..., it is what a doctor might say of someone they treated

explanation.surface: A doctor describing a smart-looking ex-patient.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the answer into MAN I CURED; the question mark flags the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Manicured means neatly kept and groomed, as is someone clean-cut.

clue.text: Sailor's small white bowl

definitions.meaning: a ..., or ... tar, is an old word for a sailor
in the game of bowls the ... is the small white ball players aim at

explanation.surface: A sailor's little white dish.
explanation.walkthrough: In lawn bowls, a British green game, players roll their bowls towards a small white target ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A jack is both a seaman and the small target ball, itself a bowl, in the game of bowls.

clue.text: Mineral component of fossil I catalogued

indicators.note: component of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A geologist naming a mineral found in a fossil they recorded.
explanation.definitionFit: Silica, silicon dioxide, is a common mineral found as quartz and flint.

clue.text: Publicity drive Queen's informally expecting

parts.note: PR, public relations, means publicity
to egg someone on is to drive them
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen; the 's adds an S

explanation.surface: A publicity campaign revealing that the Queen is expecting a baby.
explanation.definitionFit: Preggers is British slang for pregnant, which is what expecting means.

clue.text: Afflicted by rickets, misshapen bones, essentially

indicators.note: something misshapen is bent out of its form, so these letters change shape
the essence of a word is its central letter

explanation.surface: Someone suffering from rickets, with deformed bones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misshapen' rearranges RICKETS to STRICKE; 'essentially' takes N, the middle of BONES.
explanation.definitionFit: To be stricken is to be struck down by illness or trouble, so afflicted.

clue.text: In short, former Queen's Counsel finally taken on by company boss

indicators.note: being taken on by a firm puts the letter inside the boss's letters

parts.note: a CEO, chief executive officer, is a company boss

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A retired lawyer being hired by a company chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In short' shortens Cleopatra, the former queen of Egypt.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleo is the short form of Cleopatra, the last ruling queen of ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Poor writer on 13's river boat

indicators.note: in a down clue the writer sits on top of the rest

parts.note: a pen is a writing implement
13 is Cleo, Cleopatra, whose river was the Nile
SS, steamship, prefixes a boat's name

explanation.surface: An impoverished author aboard Cleopatra's river barge.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone penniless has no money at all, so is poor.

clue.text: Man's town, such as 9?

definitions.meaning: The capital town of the Isle of Man
9 is JACK, and Jack ... was an actor in the Carry On films

explanation.surface: Asking whether a man's home town resembles the sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man is a self-governing island in the Irish Sea; Jack Douglas was a British comic actor in the Carry On films.
explanation.definitionFit: Douglas is the Isle of Man's capital and the surname of the comedy actor Jack Douglas.

clue.text: Working in Canada, drunk reveals a reptile

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about, so the letters reel into a new order

parts.note: a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: A drunken worker in Canada shows a snake.
explanation.definitionFit: The anaconda is a huge South American constrictor snake, a reptile.

clue.text: Believe singer's after a drink for instructor

indicators.note: the singer's name comes after the drink

parts.note: tea is a drink
Cher had a huge hit with the song Believe

explanation.surface: A singer arriving after a drink, for her teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: A teacher is someone who instructs pupils.

clue.text: He famously explored a state capital

definitions.meaning: Christopher ... was the explorer who crossed the Atlantic in 1492
The capital of the US state of Ohio

explanation.surface: A famous explorer and a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Columbus explored the Americas, and Columbus is Ohio's capital city.

clue.text: Coils half of rope up, making a knot

parts.note: to coil is to wind, so coils means winds

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from the bottom
half of a four-letter word is its first two letters

explanation.surface: Coiling rope to tie a knot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' takes RO from ROPE and 'up' turns it to OR.
explanation.definitionFit: The Windsor is a wide, symmetrical tie knot.

clue.text: Novel introduction to extreme combat sport

indicators.note: the introduction to a word is its first letter

parts.note: MMA, mixed martial arts, is a combat sport

explanation.surface: A first look at an extreme fighting sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like an adjective meaning new, but it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Emma is a novel by Jane Austen.

clue.text: EU leader has time for country's first senior 28

indicators.note: the leader has one letter in place of another
for here means in place of, so one letter swaps for another

parts.note: Emmanuel Macron is a leader in the EU, President of France

indicators.note: the first of the word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: An EU president making time for a country's top nurse.
explanation.walkthrough: 28 is NURSE, so the definition reads 'senior nurse'.
explanation.definitionFit: A matron is the senior nurse in charge of a hospital's nursing staff.

clue.text: Doing endless exercises, fast and slow

indicators.note: exercises means the letters are worked over into a new order
without its end, the word loses its final letter

parts.note: Lent is the Christian period of fasting, a fast

explanation.surface: Exercising non-stop, quickly and then slowly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts DOING to DOIN, 'exercises' rearranges it to INDO. 'fast' looks like speed's opposite to slow, but it means Lent.
explanation.definitionFit: Indolent means lazy and sluggish, slow to act.

clue.text: Detective, one on crook's case

indicators.note: in a down clue the detective sits on top of the other piece

parts.note: DI, detective inspector, is one kind of detective

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer letters

explanation.surface: A police officer taking on a criminal's case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' takes C and K, the outside of CROOK; dick is old American slang for a detective.
explanation.definitionFit: Dick is slang, mainly American, for a private investigator.

clue.text: Climate change — has it wiped out this beast?

indicators.note: change means the letters are reordered
wiped out says some letters are removed from the pool before reordering

explanation.surface: Wondering if climate change has driven an animal to extinction.
explanation.walkthrough: Take IT out of CLIMATE and rearrange what is left, CLMAE.
explanation.definitionFit: The camel is a desert animal, which 'this beast' points to.

clue.text: Starvation diet?

parts.note: fasting is starving yourself, so a diet of fasting is jokingly called food of the fast kind

explanation.surface: A cruel eating plan.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as food for a fast: a starvation diet.
explanation.definitionFit: Burgers and chips served quickly, here punningly read as the food of someone fasting.

clue.text: Good-looking lead characters in Carry On movies — everybody loves you!

indicators.note: the lead characters of the words are their first letters

explanation.surface: An actor in Carry On films, adored by the public.
explanation.walkthrough: The Carry On films are a long-running series of cheeky British comedies.
explanation.definitionFit: Comely is an old-fashioned word for attractive.

clue.text: Guy pursuing French national, both of them short and sweet

indicators.note: both words lose their ends, so each loses its last letter
pursuing means coming after, so the guy follows

parts.note: Le Monde is a French national daily newspaper
a guy is a guy rope, steadying a tent

explanation.surface: A man chasing a Frenchman, both small and sweet-natured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'both of them short' takes the last E off LEMONDE and ROPE. 'national' suggests a person but means a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A lemon drop is a lemon-flavoured boiled sweet.

clue.text: Centrepiece of running buffet sure is tender

indicators.note: the centrepiece of a word is its middle letter
to buffet is to batter, so the letters are knocked about

explanation.surface: The central dish at a buffet is certainly succulent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buffet' and 'tender' look like food words; the first knocks SURE about, the second means one who tends.
explanation.definitionFit: A nurse tends the sick, so is a tender in the sense of one who looks after.
